prompts.text: Name something you drink out of

items.quip: A two-handled Scottish cup for sharing whisky.
items.title: Quaich
items.extract: A quaich, archaically quaigh or quoich, is a special kind of shallow two-handled drinking cup or bowl traditional in Scotland. It derives from the Scottish Gaelic cuach, meaning a cup.

prompts.text: Name a fruit with a core

items.quip: Medieval England ate it only after letting it rot on the shelf.
items.title: Mespilus germanica
items.extract: Mespilus germanica, known as the medlar or common medlar, is a large shrub or small tree in the rose family Rosaceae. When the genus Mespilus is included in the genus Crataegus, the correct name for this species is Crataegus germanica (L.) Kuntze.

prompts.text: Name a film directed by Wes Anderson

items.quip: Eight minutes for Prada in which a crashed racer meets his ancestors.
items.title: Castello Cavalcanti
items.extract: Castello Cavalcanti is a 2013 short film written and directed by Wes Anderson, starring Jason Schwartzman as an unsuccessful race car driver who crashes his car in an Italian village. The 8-minute film was filmed at Cinecittà in Rome, Italy and financed by Prada. It debuted at the Rome Film Festival and was released online on November 13, 2013. It quickly became popular and received critical acclaim.

prompts.text: Name something in a first aid kit

items.quip: An army medic designed it so a wounded soldier could wrap one-handed.
items.title: Emergency Bandage
items.extract: The Emergency Bandage or Israeli bandage is a specially designed, pressure bandage that is used to stop bleeding from hemorrhagic wounds caused by traumatic injuries in pre-hospital emergency situations. First used for saving lives during a NATO peacekeeping operation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the bandage was successfully used during operations Enduring Freedom and Iraqi Freedom. The bandage was nicknamed "Israeli bandage" by American soldiers and has been "the bandage of choice for the US Army and special forces." The Israeli Bandage was included in the first aid kits of emergency personnel and first responders at the 2011 Tucson shooting, and was used to treat some victims of the shooting.

items.quip: Horace Fletcher wanted each mouthful chewed until it liquefied.
items.title: Horace Fletcher
items.extract: Horace Fletcher was an American food faddist who earned the nickname "The Great Masticator" for his argument that food should be chewed thoroughly until liquefied before swallowing: "Nature will castigate those who don't masticate." He made elaborate justifications for this claim.

prompts.text: Name a country with an animal on its flag

items.quip: Its reverse side carries a lion nobody sees from the front.
items.title: Paraguay
items.extract: Paraguay, officially the Republic of Paraguay, is a landlocked country located in the central region of South America. It borders Bolivia to the northwest and north, Brazil to the northeast and east, and Argentina to the southeast, south, and west. Paraguay has access to the Atlantic Ocean via the Paraná–Paraguay Waterway, a system of navigable channels shared by five countries. The country is governed as a unitary presidential republic composed of a capital district and seventeen departments. Its capital and largest city is Asunción. It dates its independence from Spain to 1811.
